 import plotly.graph_objects as go
import pandas as pd

data = {
    'Factor': [
        'Lack of School Fees', 'Teacher Shortages', 'Distance to School', 'Child Labor Demand',
        'Early Marriage', 'Poor School Quality', 'Lack of Supplies', 'Health Issues',
        'Parental Education Level', 'Household Poverty', 'Cultural Norms', 'Conflict/Displacement',
        'School Safety Concerns', 'Language Barriers', 'Gender Discrimination', 'Seasonal Migration',
        'Overcrowded Classrooms', 'Lack of Sanitation', 'Transportation Costs', 'Climate-Related Disruptions'
    ],
    'IncreaseDropoutRate': [
        35.2, 28.7, 22.4, 31.5, 26.8, 20.1, 18.3, 14.6,
        19.8, 32.9, 24.5, 27.6, 16.7, 13.2, 21.9, 15.4,
        17.8, 12.3, 19.5, 11.8
    ],
    'DecreaseDropoutRate': [
        5.3, 3.8, 7.2, 4.1, 2.9, 6.5, 5.7, 8.9,
        9.2, 3.6, 4.7, 2.4, 7.8, 10.3, 5.1, 8.6,
        6.2, 9.5, 6.9, 10.5
    ],
    'Region': [
        'East Africa']*5 + ['West Africa']*5 + ['Southern Africa']*5 + ['Central Africa']*5
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

fig = go.Figure()

fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    y=df['Factor'],
    x=df['IncreaseDropoutRate'],
    name='Factors Increasing Dropout Rate',
    mode='lines+markers',
    marker=dict(color='#636EFA'),
    hovertemplate='%{y}: %{x:.1f}%<extra></extra>'
))

fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    y=df['Factor'],
    x=-df['DecreaseDropoutRate'],
    name='Factors Decreasing Dropout Rate',
    mode='lines+markers',
    marker=dict(color='#EF553B'),
    hovertemplate='%{y}: %{x:.1f}%<extra></extra>'
))

fig.update_layout(
    title='Key Factors Affecting School Dropout Rates Across African Regions (2023)',
    xaxis_title='Impact on Dropout Rate (%)',
    yaxis_title='Contributing Factors',
    barmode='relative',
    bargap=0.1,
    height=800,
    width=1000,
    plot_bgcolor='white',
    hovermode='y',
    legend=dict(
        orientation="h",
        yanchor="bottom",
        y=1.02,
        xanchor="right",
        x=1
    )
)

fig.update_xaxes(
    tickvals=[-30, -20, -10, 0, 10, 20, 30, 40],
    ticktext=['30', '20', '10', '0', '10', '20', '30', '40']
)

fig.write_image("output.png", scale=3)

The chart uses a clear color distinction—red for increasing dropout rates and blue for decreasing dropout rates—making it easy to differentiate between the two categories at a glance. from pathlib import Path
source = Path("chart.py").read_text()
source = source.replace("go.Scatter(", "go.Bar(")
source = source.replace("mode='lines+markers',", "orientation='h',")
source = source.replace("marker=dict(color='#636EFA'),", "marker=dict(color='__RED__'),")
source = source.replace("marker=dict(color='#EF553B'),", "marker=dict(color='#636EFA'),")
source = source.replace("marker=dict(color='__RED__'),", "marker=dict(color='#EF553B'),")
Path("chart.py").write_text(source)
exec(compile(source, "chart.py", "exec"))
table = pd.read_csv("table.csv")
import numpy as np
assert df['Factor'].tolist() == table['Factor'].tolist()
assert np.allclose(fig.data[0].x, table['IncreaseDropoutRate'])
assert np.allclose(fig.data[1].x, -table['DecreaseDropoutRate'])
for trace in fig.data:
    print(trace.name, trace.type, trace.orientation, trace.marker.color)
print("Layout:", fig.layout.title.text, fig.layout.width, fig.layout.height, fig.layout.barmode)
